title: Seeking ChatGPT or LLM specialist to write a bunch of articles
description: Hi,I am seeking a ChatGPT or just about any LLM specialist to craft AI-generated articles on a list of keywords that I give you. I currently have a list of about 32 keywords that I am trying to target and I need you to use your preferred tool of choice to write a [PHONE] word entry for each of them. You need to instruct your tool of choice to write the articles in a way that mentions the target keyword as much as possible without compromising on the readability of the article.At the beginning and end of the article, it should also mention the company name that provides the service the article is about and link to its site. All in all, it's a very straightforward process, just automating the writing of content marketing articles. I was doing it myself but it's getting too cumbersome submitting several prompts to ChatGPT 4.0 for each article (as it can't write 2000-3000 word articles in one-go, you have to break them into separate sections and them combine them afterwards).Please also make sure that the articles aren't written too generically. You want part of your prompt engineering to include the act of instructing it to write in a more human manner that will relate to the readers, otherwise it'll just end up writing the articles in a way that is now easily detectable as AI-generated content by most people.I've found that finding content relevant to the keyword online and copy-and-pasting/feeding it the information from those articles makes it so it doesn't give you the most generic information imaginable. You just tell it to then re-write it in a fashion that sounds more human and it will do a relatively good job of that. Then just have it insert the company in one of the paragraphs in the introduction and conclusion. The introduction needs to be subtle and relevant, I do not want the articles coming off as too "salesy".I am looking to pay $3 per finished article and will have probably another couple hundred keywords that I'll need to target in the near future. Assuming you can churn out a finished article every 10-15 minutes like I was doing, this job will be paying about $12-$18 an hour. Send your proposals my way if you are interested.Budget: $100Posted On: February 18, 2024 20:02 UTCCategory: Creative WritingSkills:Content Writing,     Search Engine Optimization,     Article Writing,     English,     Article,     Blog Content,     Writing,     Blog Writing,     SEO WritingSkills:        Content Writing,                     Search Engine Optimization,                     Article Writing,                     English,                     Article,                     Blog Content,                     Writing,                     Blog Writing,                     SEO WritingCountry: United Statesclick to apply

Expectedly, inanimate do not move.•	Each living entity has a measure of its health, represented using an integer value between 0 and 100 and all the living entities can move.  There are three types of living entities: dragons represented by the symbol #, human beings represented by @; and monsters represented by a ' * ‘ character.  Each human being has a name, the monsters have strength represented by a number between 0 and 5.•	All the animate objects can move and their health is usually reduced when they move.•	Animate entities wandering around the worldo	Humans: The humans always move to the cell to on their right, provided that this cell is not occupied and that they are not at the edge of the room. Otherwise they move to unoccupied randomly chosen cell adjacent to their current position.  Their health is reduced by one every time that they move.o	A dragon moves to a cell that is randomly chosen from those cells that are unoccupied, and adjacent to its current position. The health of the dragon is very volatile and is reduced by a random number between 0 and 5 every time it moves.o	Monsters: A monster moves as many cells as its strength at any direction (up, down, left or right) as long as the destination is free and the monster remains within the room. For instance, the monster in position (9,3) in  with strength 5 can move to position (9,8) but it cannot move to (4,3) because the cell is occupied, the monster cannot move to any other cell because it will reach the end of the room. description: I'm looking for a dev with the following skills:Automation of business processesGoogle SheetsWordpressIntegrationsZapier/Web hooksPayment processors like StripeAPIHere’s an example of a process I'd like to create:Imagine your car broke down. You used the online store to order and pay for a tow. You chose Stripe as the payment processor. It accepted your $500 deposit and put it on "hold". The tow truck arrived and towed you to your garage. The tow truck driver submitted his final mileage/gas/time totalling $200 to the tow truck company. The tow truck company adds their $100 service fee to make a total of $300. They submit $300 as the capture amount to Stripe and receive it in their account. The tow truck company sends the driver $150 (the company keeps $50 as a service fee) and so they make $150. The remaining $200 is released back to your card as available funds. That completes it.How do they do the deposit part? It's described in Stripe's documentation here:https://stripe.com/docs/payments/place-a-hold-on-a-payment-methodIf you prefer Paypal's documentation:https://developer.paypal.com/docs/checkout/standard/customize/authorization/The request needs to come from somewhere. title: Node.js sandbox
description: Hi there -I'm looking for a javascript pro to put together a bare-bones node.js express app that gives the user a code sandbox using StackBlitz WebContainers.You can read more about WebContainers here:https://webcontainers.io/guides/introductionIt is a browser based runtime that allows the running of a node application in the browser (all local).Basically, this is a project to set up their hello-world example, but using plain javascript (not Vite), and with one extra feature (file upload)What is a code sandbox?  It's:1. Code entry: A textarea where the user can write code2. Output: An output window where the results of the code run are shown (error or successful output)3. File upload: A file upload button that allows the user to upload files to the sandbox, so that they're accessible to the code that was pasted into the code-entry boxI'm attaching a wireframe so that you can see how it works.There's not much that's complicated here - just following the StackBlitz tutorial.The deliverable is:- A node express app that displays the sandbox UI- A route that uploads files to the WebContainer- A route that runs code Posted by the user, which includes- Installing npm libs specified in the user's code- A method for the user to access files that were uploaded in their code snippet (just a path convention)- Outputs the results to the output boxThat's it. Should be fun! WebContainers are awesome.Budget: $100Posted On: February 16, 2024 05:15 UTCCategory: Full Stack DevelopmentSkills:JavaScript,     Node.js,     ExpressJSSkills:        JavaScript,                     Node.js,                     ExpressJSCountry: United Statesclick to apply
